subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: Which trusted identity may resolve a QQBot fallback approval in a direct C2C chat when neither execApprovals nor an explicit non-wildcard allowFrom entry is configured?
rationale: A direct QQBot conversation identifies its sender but does not prove that sender is the bot owner, especially when the channel accepts open or wildcard DMs; choosing a fallback approver identity is therefore a security-policy decision.

options.title: Bind to trusted request identity
options.body: Preserve command authorization and allow the callback only when it matches an explicit approver or a securely recorded owner/request-recipient identity.

options.title: Require explicit configuration
options.body: Keep these callbacks denied until the operator configures execApprovals or a non-wildcard allowFrom entry, with clearer setup or denial guidance.

options.title: Trust every C2C sender
options.body: Accept the PR’s assumption that any direct-chat sender may approve operations initiated in that chat, knowingly weakening the existing authorization boundary.

recommendation.title: Bind to trusted request identity
recommendation.body: Preserve command authorization and allow the callback only when it matches an explicit approver or a securely recorded owner/request-recipient identity.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the exact fallback-callback authorization invariant this PR proposes to relax.
